subject: EmeraldCare: SAR subset export & tailored log-sampling playbook

From: Samantha Lopez <samantha.lopez@emeraldcare.org>

Cc: EmeraldCare Legal <legal@emeraldcare.org>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SAR subset export + tailored log-sampling playbook

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. EmeraldCare is preparing a Subject Access Request (SAR) process for a pilot group of users (approx 3,200 patients across two regions). Our privacy team needs a documented procedure for extracting a "subset" SAR (only PII+associated query logs) spanning the last 18 months, plus confirmation that related ephemeral inference logs for that subset can be expunged following delivery.

Can Redwood: 1) provide a playbook that details the export fields, retention windows we can honor, and a reproducible deletion proof (checksum/timestamped manifest) for ephemeral logs, and 2) advise whether we need a temporary retention exemption for customer-scoped forensic logs while we complete the review?

Attached is a short spec outlining the fields we expect in the export (EmeraldCare_SAR_spec.xlsx). We would also prefer a breakdown of lead times per model/route (hosted vs dedicated).

Samantha Lopez
Director, Privacy & Compliance
EmeraldCare

Hi Samantha — thanks for the spec and the clear ask. We've looped in our security lead (cc'd in the next message) to confirm scope. High level: we can produce a scoped export and a deletion proof for ephemeral inference logs; the exact timeline depends on whether you need exports from Hosted versus Dedicated routes and whether you require third-party audit oversight.

Proposed next steps:
- Quick 30-min kickoff this week to confirm exact fields and sample IDs (can you share 5 example IDs?).
- We’ll draft a short "playbook" that includes: extraction query, PII mapping, manifest format, deletion proof format (signed manifest + sha256), and an activity log for the work.
- If you need a temporary exception to retain certain low-level debug logs while the SAR is processed, we’ll document the justification and required approvals (security + legal) and timebox the exception.

I’ve attached an internal SAR workflow doc we typically start from (Redwood_SAR_workflow_v1.docx) — happy to tailor. If you’re OK I’ll schedule the kickoff and include our security lead (Karthik) and Neha from SOC2.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SAR subset export + tailored log-sampling playbook

Naomi / Samantha — quick technical notes to align expectations.

1) Log tiers & feasibility:
- Ephemeral inference logs: these are short-lived by default (configurable 7–90 days depending on customer profile). For a SAR export we can reconstruct request+response pairs for the subset you specified if the traces exist in the retention window.
- Persistent audit logs: stored in cold storage for 730 days for customers on enterprise contracts; otherwise 90 days. Exports from cold storage add 1–3 business days.

2) Deletion proof approach:
- We produce a signed manifest listing exported object ids, sha256 checksums, and a deletion timestamp. For ephemeral logs we can then run the expunge job and provide a post-delete manifest showing removal from the active store. Note: immutable backups (e.g., backup vault snapshots) may require separate legal approval to destroy; we will document the retention chain.

3) Exception & approvals:
- If EmeraldCare requests a temporary extension (e.g., retain ephemeral logs for 30 additional days while legal reviews), we require: (a) written justification from customer legal, (b) security approval (me), and (c) SOC2 change log entry from Neha. We will timebox exceptions to 30 days by default.

4) Data fields for export (high level): user identifiers, timestamp, route id, request payload (redact model internals on request), generated text, model metadata, and any linked user metadata. Please confirm if you need full model inputs (we may need a more detailed assessment for potential PII in system prompts).

Quoted for context:
> "Can Redwood: 1) provide a playbook that details the export fields..." — noted, we’ll produce a draft playbook and a timeline.

I’ll prepare a draft playbook (Redwood_Log_Export_Playbook.pdf) and proposed approval checklist. Naomi — once you have the kickoff scheduled I’ll pull in engineering to scope extraction costs/timelines.

Karthik
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
